questions.question: Describe the spoon test and explain what it shows about metals.
questions.expected_answer: A metal spoon, a plastic spoon and a wooden spoon are stood in hot water. After a few minutes, the metal spoon is hot at the handle, while the others are only slightly warm. It shows that metals are good conductors of heat, and wood and plastic are insulators.

questions.question: Are all metals magnetic? Explain with examples.
questions.expected_answer: No. Only a few metals are magnetic, mainly iron and steel, and also nickel and cobalt. A steel paper clip or iron nail is attracted to a magnet, but aluminium cans, copper wire, gold and silver are not.

questions.question: What is the difference between rusting and tarnishing? Give two ways to prevent rust.
questions.expected_answer: Rusting happens only to iron and steel, when water and oxygen reach them; rust is orange-brown, flaky and weakens the metal. Tarnishing is when other metals, like silver or copper, become dull or change colour on the surface, and it can be polished off. Rust can be prevented by painting, oiling or greasing, coating with plastic, or galvanising with zinc.
